title: Kimi AskUserQuestion shows raw JSON with Approve/Reject, and Approve silently answers with the first option
outcome: A Kimi AskUserQuestion appears as a readable question card: the question in plain text and one button per answer, labelled with that answer's name. Choosing a button sends exactly that answer's optionId, and dismissing sends the reject option. No generic "Approve" ever answers a question for the user.
acceptance: The real Kimi contract is checked and recorded on this item, from a fresh capture on the current Kimi Code version or the cited kimi-code source: for AskUserQuestion, the session/request_permission params carry the question text and options, with optionId, name and kind. The note states whether each answer is an allow_once option and what reject means (skip, or dismiss).

When Kimi sends a session/request_permission that is an AskUserQuestion, or that offers more than one allow_once option, TermAl shows the question text as plain text, not raw JSON, and offers one choice per option labelled with its name. Selecting a choice sends {outcome: selected, optionId: <that option's id>}, and a dismiss or skip sends the reject option when one exists.

For such a request, TermAl never answers with whichever allow_once option happens to come first, so no single generic 'Approve' picks an answer on the user's behalf. Requests with exactly one allow_once option, such as tool permissions, keep today's Approve/Reject behaviour.

Tests check the observable behaviour from a captured-shape fixture: the rendered question and choice labels, the exact optionId sent for a non-first choice, and the reject path. The tests do not pin implementation text.
